correctness.rationale: Quotient by constants: the open first-difference map is an isometry to ℓ¹, and the unit coordinate directions lift to the single cuts. A scalar soft-threshold secant has slope in [0,1], so the effective detail multiplier lies in the convex hull of all 0/1 masks. Every vertex is realized exactly on sufficiently short segments in the corresponding strict chamber for every λ>0, including the maximizing cut. All nonstraddling details vanish, and dotting the remaining normalized detail with the cut yields −m/√s, so the response is ∓m/s as stated, including m=0 at boundaries. At most two end jumps and one interior jump give total variation at most 4m/s≤2. For even d the selected cuts at j=(2^d−1)/3 on scales k=2 mod 4, k≤d−2, have m=(2^k−1)/3, true interior block boundaries, and distinct jump positions: each finer selected block lies strictly between the left endpoint and midpoint of its next larger selected ancestor and away from both. This also separates it from all other larger ancestors. Each contributes at least one. Duplicating coordinates embeds depth d−1 without changing the coarser masked variation, and floor(d/4) is unchanged at odd d. Independent exact reproduction from dyadic conditional averages (python3 /workspace/reviews/evidence_4_5.py) obtained all eight stated numbers; it did not run the uploaded verifier. The chamber/cut arguments, not those eight values, prove the all-depth claims.
